lookForward.fits: Fat Bear Week champion crowned tomorrow, Tuesday 29 September 2026.
lookForward.headline: A champion bear is crowned tomorrow
lookForward.line: Last day of Fat Bear Week voting: Katmai National Park in Alaska asks the public which brown bear fattened up best for winter. Cast a vote at fatbearweek.org today. Somewhere in Alaska a very round animal is about to win the internet without noticing.

source.name: National Park Service: Fat Bear Week 2026

more: Katmai National Park is on the Alaska Peninsula, a place with more brown bears than people. In late summer the bears stand in the Brooks River and catch sockeye salmon as the fish leap the falls, eating as much as they can before winter. A bear that goes into its den in October will not eat again until spring, so the fatter, the better.

Fat Bear Week turns that into a game. The park picks twelve or so bears, shows a photo of each from July and one from September, and pairs them in a knockout bracket. Anyone can vote once a day at fatbearweek.org, free, no account needed. Voting runs from Tuesday 22 September to Tuesday 29 September 2026, when the champion is named. Nobody tells the bear.
The live cameras at explore.org show the Brooks Falls all day. Watch for a while; it is very calming, and the salmon are still running.

onThisDay.fits: 28 September 1924: US Army fliers completed the first flight around the world, landing in Seattle.
onThisDay.headline: The first flight around the world ended in Seattle
onThisDay.line: Four open-cockpit biplanes left Seattle in April; two came back, 175 days and 27,000 miles later. The planes are in the Smithsonian.

source.name: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum

kindness.text: Send someone a photo of the Harvest Moon from the weekend, if you took one. If you did not, describe it to them.

joke.setup: What is a bear's campaign slogan for Fat Bear Week?
joke.punchline: I have done nothing but eat, and I am proud of it.

riddle.riddle: I left Seattle in April, came back in September, and never left the ground for long. What am I?
riddle.hint: Two out of four made it.
